title: That Question in the Shade of the Ka‘bah • The Day ‘Umar (RA) Was Shown the Back • Did We Get Our Reward in This World Itself • The Day Suhayb Gave Everything • The Day Abu Dharr Stood Before the Ka‘bah • Why the Test • The People of the Ditch • The Fire That Does Not Burn Gold • Final Word

blocks.0: That Question in the Shade of the Ka‘bah
blocks.1: One day Khabbab (RA) and several Companions came to the Prophet {{1}}. He was sitting in the shade of the Ka‘bah. He had made his cloak a pillow and was reclining. That scene. A cloak. The shade of a wall. And a group of men whose bodies were full of wounds.
blocks.2: Khabbab (RA) said, will you not ask for help for us! Will you not make du‘a for us! The Prophet {{1}} sat up. His face turned red.
blocks.3: He said, among those before you there was a man who would be seized, a hole dug for him in the ground, and he would be placed in it. Then a saw would be brought and placed on his head, and he would be split in two. Yet he did not turn from his din. His flesh would be stripped from his bones with iron combs. Yet he did not turn from his din.
blocks.4: Then he said, by Allah, Allah will surely complete this matter. A day will come when a rider will travel alone from San‘a to Hadramawt, with no fear in his heart of anyone but Allah; at most the fear of a wolf for his goats.
blocks.5: At the end he said, but you are in a hurry.{{1}}
blocks.6: He did not make du‘a. The one at whose du‘a rain would fall from the sky, did not make du‘a for these men. Why! Because this hardship had a work to do.
blocks.7: He had been angry. His face had turned red. Angry at whom! Not at Khabbab (RA). The anger was at an idea inside the question. The idea was this; if you follow the din, there will be no hardship.
blocks.8: He broke that very idea. He said, there were people before you too; they were cut in two with saws. That is, there is hardship on this path. There was, and there will be. But at the same moment he said another thing. This will end.
blocks.9: Two things together. Hardship will remain, and victory will surely come. We often take one and drop the other. One speaks only of hardship; people become despondent. One speaks only of victory; people go in without preparation, then break down at the first blow.
blocks.10: The Prophet {{1}} said both, in the same breath. ‘But you are in a hurry.’ The words touch us too. We make du‘a, and sit watching the clock. A week. A month. A year. Then we say, it did not happen.
blocks.11: We think du‘a is a button; press it and the thing is done. What Khabbab (RA) asked for that day, he got. But not at once. He lived. He saw the conquest of Makkah. He saw the fall of Rome and Persia. He lived to see that rider able to go alone from San‘a to Hadramawt.
blocks.12: It only took time. Allah’s clock does not match our clock. On our clock thirteen years is a large part of a life. By Allah’s reckoning thirteen years is the time of laying a foundation.
blocks.13: A foundation laid in haste, nothing stands on it. What is haste, really! Haste means not accepting Allah’s timetable. I decide when the thing should happen. Then if it does not happen on that date, I assume it will not.
blocks.14: Yet I do not know when the thing is good to happen. I do not know whether getting it today would have been good for me, or harm. A small example. If the child asks today and the father gives tomorrow, the boy thinks, father did not give. The father knows that giving it today would have harmed the boy.
blocks.15: We are that boy. The difference is, the father’s knowledge is limited; and the One we are asking has infinite knowledge.
blocks.16: The Day ‘Umar (RA) Was Shown the Back
blocks.17: This is from many years later. ‘Umar (RA) was then the caliph. The capital of Islam, Madinah. Rome and Persia had both collapsed. One day Khabbab (RA) came to him.
blocks.18: ‘Umar (RA) seated him in his own seat. He said, in this world only one man had more right to this seat; Bilal. Khabbab (RA) said, why, Amir al-Mu’minin!
blocks.19: Then in the course of talk he uncovered his back and showed it. ‘Umar (RA) kept looking. He said, I have never seen a back like this. Khabbab (RA) said, I used to be laid on the fire. That fire would not go out until the fat of my back melted and flowed down.{{1}}
blocks.20: There is something here. Year after year has passed. Islam has won. But the mark has not gone. Those who won, the price of winning was written on their bodies. We have received the state of having won. We have not paid the price.
blocks.21: Did We Get Our Reward in This World Itself
blocks.22: In his last years Khabbab (RA) became well off. A house, wealth. And seeing it he would weep. He would say, we migrated with the Prophet {{1}} only for the pleasure of Allah. Our reward with Allah had become fixed.
blocks.23: Then he would speak of Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA). He was martyred on the day of Uhud. There was only one cloak to shroud him. If the head was covered, the feet came out. If the feet were covered, the head came out.
blocks.24: The Prophet {{1}} said, cover the head, and put idhkhir grass over the feet. Khabbab (RA) would say, some of us have gone, without enjoying any of their fruit in this world. And the fruit of some of us has ripened; he is now gathering it.{{2}}
blocks.25: A fear lies hidden inside those words. He was afraid, was my reward given to me in this world itself! We fear exactly the opposite. We fear, why did I get nothing in this world. He feared, why did I get in this world.
blocks.26: The whole difference lies between these two fears. Here one thing needs to be made clear. Being well off in this world is not a fault. Having wealth is not a fault. Khabbab (RA) did not throw wealth away. He was only afraid, lest the account be settled here.
blocks.27: This fear is what keeps a believer moving. The one who has nothing thinks; Allah has forgotten me. The one who has everything thinks; Allah loves me. Both are wrong reckonings.
blocks.28: Wealth is one form of test, want is also one form of test. The question is not what I got; the question is what I did with what I got.
blocks.30: Let me name one more. Suhayb ibn Sinan (RA). He had lived as a captive in Rome, then came to Makkah, and built wealth through trade. Everyone knew him by the name ‘Suhayb al-Rumi’.
blocks.31: He too accepted Islam. Persecution came down on him too; because he too had no tribe. Later at the time of the Hijrah, when he took the road to Madinah, the Quraysh stood blocking the way.
blocks.32: They said, you came penniless, you built wealth here with us. Now you will take it all and go! That will not happen. He said, well, if I give you all my wealth, will you clear the way!
blocks.33: They said, we will. He gave everything. He began walking toward Madinah empty-handed. When he reached Madinah, the Prophet {{1}} saw him and said, the deal was profitable, O Abu Yahya! The deal was profitable!{{2}}
blocks.34: The savings of a whole life gone in a moment. And he walked on with a smile. Because the one who knows what he is buying does not haggle over the price.
blocks.35: The Day Abu Dharr Stood Before the Ka‘bah
blocks.36: Let me speak of another; this one was not a slave. Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA). A man of the tribe of Ghifar; they carried no special weight with Makkah. He had come to Makkah in search of the truth. He met the Prophet {{1}}, and accepted Islam at once.
blocks.37: The Prophet {{1}} told him, now go back to your tribe. Do not say this openly. Abu Dharr (RA) did not listen. He went straight to al-Masjid al-Haram, stood in the midst of the crowd, raised his voice and said, I bear witness that there is no deity but Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
blocks.38: The Quraysh pounced. Beating him, they threw him to the ground. ‘Abbas came and bent over him. He said, what are you doing! This is a man of Ghifar; the trade route to Sham is in their hands. Let him go.{{1}}
blocks.39: The next day Abu Dharr (RA) did the same thing again. Was beaten again. Again ‘Abbas saved him. No one forced him. Hiding would have been enough. But the thing he had found did not seem to him something to keep behind a closed mouth.
blocks.40: Today we often walk the opposite way. Even the little that cannot but be said we swallow; lest someone think something. For Abu Dharr (RA) the din was such a thing that one who finds it cannot stay silent.
blocks.42: After all we have heard, one question is natural. Could Allah not have stopped all this! He could. In one moment He could. Then why did He let it happen! The answer is in the Qur’an itself
blocks.44: Alif-Lam-Mim. Do people think that merely by saying ‘We have believed’ they will be left without being tested? Yet We tested those who passed before them as well. So Allah will surely find out who showed truthfulness, and He will surely find out who are the liars.{{1}}
blocks.45: There is a hard thing inside the verse. Saying ‘we have believed’ is no proof. Anyone can say it with the mouth. In easy times everyone says it. But what faith really is, that is known only when a price has to be paid for it.
blocks.46: The one who lies on the burning sand and says ‘Ahad’, his word is proven. The one who says it sitting in an air-conditioned room, his word has not yet been tested. Test does not mean punishment. Test means verification.
blocks.47: To verify gold it must be put in the fire. The fire is not the enemy of the gold; it is the enemy of the dross. There is another side. The test is not only verification; it is also forming. The ummah that is to lead the world has to be formed first.
blocks.48: What did Allah form in these thirteen years of Makkah! Some people who do not change their word even at the price of their lives. Later it was at the hands of these very people that Rome and Persia collapsed.
blocks.49: People formed in easy times can do easy work. For hard work, people formed in hard times are needed. So the hardship was not punishment. It was training.
blocks.51: There is another scene in the Qur’an; of those who believed before us. A kingdom. A tyrant king. And a group of people who had acknowledged the One Allah. The king had long trenches dug by the roadside. The trenches were filled with fire. Then it was announced; whoever will not give up faith will be thrown into this fire.
blocks.52: Not one stepped back. One by one they were thrown into that fire. And the king and his men sat at the edge of the pit and watched.
blocks.54: May Allah’s curse be on the people of the ditch, the people of the fire full of fuel. When they were sitting beside it and were watching what they were doing to the believers. They were punishing the believers only because they had believed in that Allah, who is possessed of great power, worthy of all praise.{{1}}
blocks.56: The last word of the verse is important here. ‘Only because they had believed in Allah.’ The offence was one. When a man steals he is punished, when he kills he is punished; that is understandable. But here the offence was belief.
blocks.57: In this one place Jahiliyyah is always the same. It can tolerate the thief, but it cannot tolerate the one who is unwilling to bow his head.
blocks.58: The Fire That Does Not Burn Gold
blocks.59: In the story of the People of the Ditch there is a thing not everyone notices. None of them survived. No angel came down. The fire did not turn cold. The king’s throne did not fall. All of them burned.
blocks.60: And Allah kept the story in the Qur’an. Right here an idea of ours needs breaking. We think, if faith is right, the trouble will pass. The illness will be cured. The job will come through.
blocks.61: But Allah has promised this nowhere. He has promised that He is watching. And keeping the account. Sumayyah (RA) did not survive. The people of the Ditch did not survive. Yet they are the ones who won. Because the definition of winning is not in our hands.
blocks.62: One more thing. We make du‘a, ‘O Allah, remove the trouble’. The du‘a is fine; we must make it. But another du‘a needs to be added alongside. ‘O Allah, if You do not remove the trouble, hold me firm.’
blocks.63: The first du‘a is about the situation. The second is about oneself. The situation does not always change. One can always be held firm.
blocks.65: In today’s dars we heard of a few people. Bilal, who had a rock on his chest and one word on his lips. Zinnirah, whose eyes were gone and whose argument was not. Sumayyah, who gave the first blood. ‘Ammar, who said it with his mouth and yet held his heart. Khabbab, whose back-scars stayed until death. Suhayb, who gave the savings of a whole life in one sentence.
blocks.66: Not one of them was a big man then. Slave, slave-woman, outsider, blacksmith. Those whose names were not in the ledger of Makkah. And today! No one names a son Abu Jahl. No one names a son Umayyah. No one names a son al-‘As ibn Wa’il.
blocks.67: But in millions of homes of the world even today sons are named Bilal. ‘Ammar. Khabbab. Suhayb. The names of those who beat have been wiped out. The names of those who were beaten remain.
blocks.68: This is Allah’s reckoning. And there is one more thing. None of them knew that their names would remain. Bilal (RA), lying on the sand, did not think that fourteen hundred years later in some home in Bangladesh a boy would be born with my name.
blocks.69: He only held on to one word. The rest Allah did. In the coming dars we shall see what happened when this persecution went beyond endurance; the first Hijrah, to Abyssinia, and the acceptance of Islam in Makkah by two men, which changed the whole reckoning.
blocks.70: So take one task from today’s dars. From now on speak of your hardship not in gatherings but on the prayer mat. Ya‘qub (AS) laid his grief and sorrow before Allah right there.
blocks.72: Under Bilal’s (RA) back, scorching sand; on his chest, a rock. On his lips one word only; Ahad. Today I will ask myself one question: what price have I paid for my kalimah?
blocks.73: From today I will speak of hardship not to people but on the prayer mat, which from today I will not give up.

footnotes.0: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3612 and 6943; from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (RA). Verified on hadithunlocked.com (bukhari:3612). Concerning the plea of the Companions in the shade of the Ka‘bah, the account by the Prophet {{1}} of the persecution of earlier communities, the prophecy of travelling safely from San‘a to Hadramawt, and the words ‘but you are in a hurry’. This is at once a lesson in sabr and a clear sign of prophethood.
footnotes.1: The severe persecution of Khabbab (RA) is clear in the context of Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3612 itself. As for the scene “‘Umar (RA) seated him beside himself and said, only one man is worthy of this seat; then Khabbab (RA) uncovered his back and showed the scars”, it is the narration of Ibn Sa‘d, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, 3/116–118 and al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak; there is discussion about the chain. This part is used as a scene, not as proof.
footnotes.2: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 1276 and 4047; from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (RA). Verified on hadithunlocked.com (bukhari:1276). Concerning the difficulty of the shroud of Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA) and the saying ‘the fruit of some of us has ripened, he is gathering it’.
footnotes.3: The Companionship of Suhayb ibn Sinan (RA) and his standing are established by sound chains. As for the part “at the time of the Hijrah the Quraysh stopped him, he obtained permission to go in exchange for all his wealth, and the Prophet {{1}} on hearing it said, rabiha al-bay‘, Aba Yahya; the deal was profitable, O Abu Yahya”, it is narrated in Ibn Ishaq; Sirah Ibn Hisham; al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak; Ibn Sa‘d, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra; some chains have been called hasan, some mursal. The incident belongs to the Hijrah period; here it is brought briefly only by way of introducing Suhayb (RA), with details in the dars on the Hijrah.
footnotes.4: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 3522; Sahih Muslim, hadith 2474. The acceptance of Islam by Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA), the advice of the Prophet {{1}} to him to keep it secret, his giving open testimony of the kalimah in al-Masjid al-Haram, the beating by the Quraysh, the same incident again the next day, and the intervention of ‘Abbas; all are narrated by sound chains in this long hadith.
footnotes.7: The detailed account of the People of the Ditch comes in Sahih Muslim, hadith 3005 (the long hadith of the boy, the monk and the sorcerer). It should be noted that in the note of Tafsir Tawdih al-Qur’an it is said that the narration of Muslim does not state explicitly that the people of the ditch in Surah al-Buruj are the people of this very incident; this link was made by Muhammad ibn Ishaq (RH). So the statement of the verse is definitive, while the detailed form of the incident is report-based.

quiz.q: In the shade of the Ka‘bah, what did Khabbab (RA) ask of the Prophet ﷺ?
o: Permission to leave Makkah
Permission to fight the Quraysh
Du‘a and help for us
Permission to carry on deeds in secret
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ was then sitting reclined on his cloak. He sat up, his face turned red, and he spoke of the persecution of earlier communities.

quiz.q: What persecution of earlier believers did the Prophet ﷺ mention?
o: Drowned in the sea, and houses all burned
Placed in a pit and split with a saw, flesh stripped with iron combs
Driven from the city and all wealth seized
Paraded in the market, humiliated and imprisoned
quiz.e: Yet they would not turn from the din. With it he said, this work will be completed; a rider will go from San‘a to Hadramawt, with no fear of anyone but Allah.

quiz.q: What was the reason for the face of the Prophet ﷺ turning red in the shade of the Ka‘bah?
o: The insolence of Khabbab (RA)
Hearing news of fresh oppression by the Quraysh
The idea ‘if you follow the din there will be no hardship’
Seeing the impatience of the Companions
quiz.e: He broke that very idea. In the same breath he said two things; there will be hardship on this path, and this will surely be completed.

quiz.q: When du‘a seems to bring no result, which point does the dars recall?
o: The words of the du‘a must be changed
More sadaqah must be given
Allah’s clock is not our clock
Du‘a must be dropped and effort begun
quiz.e: Khabbab (RA) got what he asked for, but not at once. A foundation laid in haste, nothing stands on it.

quiz.q: What did the dars mean by the analogy ‘the child asks today, the father gives tomorrow’?
o: There can be good even behind the delay
Merely a method of teaching patience
Teaching the right manner of asking
Explaining the child’s right over the father
quiz.e: The boy thinks the father did not give; the father knows that giving today would have harmed him. The difference is, the father’s knowledge is limited, while the One we ask has infinite knowledge.

quiz.q: What problem arose with the shroud of Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA)?
o: No cloth could be found that day
None of the Companions came forward to shroud him
The cloth was so costly it could not be used
Covering the head with one cloak left the feet out
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ said, cover the head and put idhkhir grass over the feet. Khabbab (RA) would weep telling this incident.

quiz.q: Why did Khabbab (RA) weep after becoming well off?
o: Remembering the hardships of old days again and again
Whether he had received his reward in this world itself
Out of fear of losing his wealth
Feeling the absence of old companions
quiz.e: We fear, why did I get nothing in this world. He feared, why did I get in this world. The whole difference lies between the two fears.

quiz.q: What does the dars say about measuring Allah’s love by wealth or want?
o: Having wealth is proof of Allah’s love
Having want is proof of Allah’s displeasure
Both are tests; the question is what I did
Keeping wealth is itself the fault
quiz.e: The one who has nothing thinks Allah has forgotten him, the one who has everything thinks Allah loves him; both are wrong reckonings.

quiz.q: What did Suhayb ibn Sinan (RA) do at the time of the Hijrah?
o: Slipped out secretly in the dark of night
Gave up all his wealth and got the way
Made a treaty with the Quraysh
Mingled with a caravan
quiz.e: The Quraysh blocked the way and said, you came penniless, built wealth, and now will take it all! He gave everything. The Prophet ﷺ said, the deal was profitable, O Abu Yahya!

quiz.q: Despite the advice of the Prophet ﷺ to keep it secret, what did Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA) do?
o: Openly testified to the kalimah before the Ka‘bah
Quietly returned to his tribe
Went to the houses of the Quraysh leaders and called them in secret
Migrated to Abyssinia
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ had asked him to keep it secret; Abu Dharr (RA) raised his voice in al-Masjid al-Haram amid the crowd and testified, was beaten for two days, and ‘Abbas saved him.

quiz.q: According to Surah al-‘Ankabut, why is merely saying ‘we have believed’ not enough?
o: Faith shows itself only in action
The words must be said in Arabic
Because no one’s word is acceptable without witnesses
The word of the mouth can be said by anyone in easy times
quiz.e: What faith is, is known only when a price has to be paid for it. Test is not punishment, it is verification; the fire is not the enemy of gold, it is the enemy of the dross.

quiz.q: According to Surah al-Buruj, what was the ‘offence’ of the believers of the ditch?
o: They had directly disobeyed the king’s order
Only believing in Allah
They had organised in secret
They had opposed the sorcerer
quiz.e: The words of the verse: ‘only because they had believed in Allah’. Jahiliyyah tolerates the thief, but cannot tolerate the one who does not bow his head.

quiz.q: If the trouble does not pass, which additional du‘a does the dars ask us to add?
o: Cursing the enemy
Hold me firm even if You do not remove it
Praying for a quick solution
Having someone else make du‘a
quiz.e: The first du‘a is about the situation, the second about oneself. The situation does not always change; one can always be held firm.

quiz.q: What is the practical resolve of this dars?
o: Reading one page of the Sirah daily
Giving a little sadaqah at least daily
Not missing the prayers I skip out of laziness
Memorising the names of the persecuted Companions
quiz.e: The first demand of the kalimah that Bilal (RA) held on to with a rock on his chest is prayer.

quiz.q: What is the biggest lesson from the names of those who beat being wiped out?
o: Allah’s reckoning is exact, even if late
The tyrant is always destroyed quickly
Learning the rules for naming children
History tells only of the victors
quiz.e: Today in millions of homes sons are named Bilal, ‘Ammar, Khabbab, Suhayb; no one names a son Abu Jahl or Umayyah. None of them knew their names would remain.
